name: Max Healthcare Institute Ltd.
business_summary: Premium multi-speciality hospital chain, North India-heavy (Delhi NCR, Mohali, Dehradun, Lucknow) with Mumbai/Nagpur and Bengaluru-Jaipur expansion; ~5,000+ operational beds (model knowledge) and Max Lab diagnostics. Highest ARPOB among listed peers and EBITDA margin ~27%. Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue +20% YoY, consolidated PAT Rs 414 cr (-15%, after higher depreciation/interest and a prior-year gain; Zee Business 2026-10-30), network PAT Rs 448 cr (+10%). Pack figures (sales Rs 2,569 cr, EBITDA Rs 711 cr) differ from the 'network' scope (Q1 network sales Rs 2,982 cr, EBITDA Rs 704 cr, Healthcare Executive 2026-08-14) - scope difference, use growth rates. Mcap Rs 90,369 cr, P/E 64, FIIs 40.5%.

revenue_mix.geography: India; Delhi NCR ~50%+, Punjab/Uttarakhand, Mumbai, Lucknow (model knowledge)

exposures.mechanism: Stock fell ~20% in 3 weeks to a 2-year low (Business Standard 2026-10-13) after SC remarks on markups (2026-09-30) and Centre's 30% cancer-drug price cut. Pharmacy/consumables ~22% of network revenue; oncology (Max's strongest speciality ~20% of revenue) drug markup contribution ~2% of revenue at ~100% drop-through -> -7.5% EBITDA at 27% OPM per step; EV/MCap 1.08, persistence 1.0 but 40% mitigated by procedure repricing -> -4.9; add MRP-cap broadening risk -> -6.0. Max MD: 'hospital pricing part of wider value chain' (ET 2026-10-06).

evidence.note: Max Healthcare slips 20% in 3 weeks; SC seeks 16% MRP cap (ET 2026-09-30)

exposures.mechanism: Employee+doctor fees ~38% of costs. +2pp wage inflation = +0.76% of costs; 55% passed through -> +0.34% of costs = 0.25% of revenue (costs ~73%); / 27% OPM = EBITDA -0.9%; EV/MCap 1.08, persistence 1.0 -> -1.0.

Premium elective/high-acuity and international patients are tied to urban affluence/insurance. +5pp urban demand -> +2.5pp revenue at 55% incremental margin vs 27% base -> +5% EBITDA; EV/MCap 1.08, persistence 0.5 -> +2.7; haircut for 70-75% occupancy -> +2.2.

evidence.note: CLSA eyes upside on hospital expansion, margin (Moneycontrol 2026-11-04)

exposures.mechanism: Interest Rs 74 cr/qtr (TTM Rs 271 cr) vs EBITDA Rs 2,455 cr; +25bp = Rs 3 cr = 0.1% EBITDA; main channel is discount rate on 64x P/E: duration ~16 yrs, +25bp -> -2.0.
FII holding 40.5% (down from 45.4% in Mar-26); beta 1.23-1.29. +US$5bn inflow -> broad +4% x beta 1.25 + re-positioning of an FII-owned stock -> +3.5 beyond market move.

International patients ~8% of revenue (model knowledge) and imported equipment/consumables offset; +3% -> +0.4% sales... net +0.3% EBITDA; empirical +1.67 (t=0.8), correlation likely FPI-related -> +1.0.

Empirical DXY +3.26 (t=2.5) is positive, contradicting expectation that strong USD hurts FIIs holding 40%; likely spurious (period-specific). Model prior: +3% DXY = FPI outflow -> -1.5, shrunk from data (the sign conflict is flagged).

evidence.note: Pack: DXY +3.26 (t=2.5) sign conflict with prior

exposures.mechanism: Hospital volumes +4-5% of GDP elasticity 0.6; +1pp GDP -> +0.6% volume -> +1.2% EBITDA, persistence 1.0 -> +1.3; rerating -> +1.6.
Oncology, transplants, robotics and international patients lift ARPOB ~6%/yr; +1 theme unit -> +1.8.
